- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) in the recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent high.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) in recent days, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to compensate for bearish bias.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 1–3% for first 5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–15 day window; if forecast is > 80% above 10-day moving average, reduce by 1–2%.
- Sentiment history with 1.00 (strong bullish) followed by 0.00 (neutral) often leads to overcorrection; adjust forecast downward by 2–4% after such transitions.
